title: OCR hyphenation & broken-token repair — labeler notebook
body:
Purpose / quick context:
This is a personal scratchpad for heuristics and examples I keep referring to when cleaning OCR outputs before passing data to human annotators or the labeling pipeline. Many sources we ingest (scanned contracts, receipts, tech docs) have line-break hyphenation and other broken-token artifacts that confuse span-based labels and tokenizers.

Goal:
- Enumerate common OCR hyphenation patterns and ambiguous cases.
- Draft conservative automatic repair rules we can run pre-labeling (and tests to validate them).
- Provide examples for labelers and a decision tree for ambiguous merges so human reviewers can be consistent.

Observed patterns (notes from sample batches):
- Line-break hyphenation: tokens split with a hyphen at end of line, e.g. "trans-\nfer" -> should be "transfer". Very common in multi-column scanned PDFs.
- Compounds with legitimate hyphens: e.g. "well-known", "state-of-the-art" (should stay as-is).
- Soft hyphens / U+00AD sneaking in from OCR outputs and causing invisible break characters.
- Broken punctuation leading to trailing hyphen: e.g. "pre-\n," or "re-\n: options" — OCR sometimes inserts punctuation tokens on next line.
- Affix splits vs morphological splits: "co-\noperate" (cooperate) vs "re-\nenter" (reenter) — both should merge.
- Non-English cases: German compound nouns often legitimately hyphenated across lines; careful with language detection.
- Hyphen at start of line (bullet lists): "- installation" vs word-fragment hyphenation.

Heuristic rules (ranked conservative -> aggressive):
1) Invisible/soft hyphen removal: first pass remove U+00AD and similar invisible marks globally.
2) Line-break hyphenation merge: pattern: ([a-zA-Z0-9]+)-\n([a-zA-Z0-9]+) -> merge to single token unless either side is single-letter AND left side is capitalized? (edge).
   - Implement with context window: if both parts alphabetic and combined length >= 3 then merge.
3) Preserve explicit hyphenated tokens with internal spaces intact (i.e., do NOT merge tokens already separated by spaces or with hyphen but no newline): "well-known" stays.
4) Punctuation reattachment: patterns like ([a-z]) -\n, -> combine to ([a-z],) but re-evaluate spacing. If punctuation belongs to following token ("re-\n: value") then reformat to "re: value" — heuristics to detect punctuation-only next tokens.
5) Number tokens and identifiers: if split inside digits or alphanumeric IDs like "AB12-\n34" -> merge always.
6) Language-aware rule: if language detect == "de" (German) and hyphenation matches known morphological breakpoints (we don't have dictionary yet) -> defer to human or use conservative merge.

Examples (before -> after, with labeling notes):
- "trans-\nfer request approved" -> "transfer request approved" (merge; label spans that include "transfer" should be contiguous)
- "well-\nknown issue" -> "well-known issue" (should we keep hyphen? prefer keep because compound adjective)
- "it is a re-\nentry protocol" -> "it is a reentry protocol" (merge, remove hyphen)
- "Qty: 1,234-\n567" -> "Qty: 1,234567" (bad: for numbers we should insert digit join without comma removal — better rule: merge numeric groups and then re-normalize to standard thousand separators)
- "co-\noperate with partner" -> "cooperate with partner"

Decision flow (for labeler handoff):
- If OCR has explicit line-break hyphen ("-\n") and both left/right tokens are alphabetic and combined length >= 4 -> auto-merge.
- If one side is punctuation or numeral -> run numeric/identifier merge rule.
- If combined token is in a small blacklist of known hyphenated compounds (e.g., "X-ray", "T-shirt") -> keep hyphen. Maintain "keep-hyphen" whitelist.
- Ambiguous: flag for human review with a short hint message: "possible hyphenation across line break — please decide: merge / keep hyphen / split". Show 3 tokens of context on both sides.

Regex prototypes (for pipeline devs) — not final code, just notes:
- soft hyphen cleaner: s/\u00AD//g
- line-break merge: s/([A-Za-z0-9]{2,})-\n([A-Za-z0-9]{2,})/\1\2/g
- numeric merge: s/([0-9])-\n([0-9])/$1$2/g (then run thousand-sep normalizer)
- preserve hyphenated words: detect if token contains '-' and NOT followed/preceded by newline -> leave as is

Known pitfalls / edge cases to watch: 
- Acronym splits: "U-\nS" -> probably should be "US" but capitalize rules matter (don't lower-case).
- Hyphenation that crosses morphological boundary changing meaning: e.g. "re-\ncover" -> "recover" (ok) vs "re-\ncover" where original text had space: 're- cover' unlikely though.
- Scanned tables and column wrap: merging across columns will create nonsensical tokens if algorithm doesn't check for column boundaries. We need column detection heuristics (x-position metadata) or conservative rule requiring left and right words to be in same OCR block.
- Hyphen used as bullet vs fragmentation: leading '-' followed by space should be recognized as list bullet and not a hyphenated token.

Human labeling guidance (short):
- If flagged, prefer permissive merge that produces English words unless the merged token looks unnatural (lots of repeated consonants, non-dictionary) — then mark 'needs correction'.
- For entity spans: when merging, ensure span indexes shift consistently (we need to publish a small script for label UI to remap spans after auto-merge).
- Document examples for labelers: show 5 typical merges and 3 intentionally ambiguous ones.

Test ideas (quick):
- Create 200 synthetic line-break samples from a text corpus: insert '-\n' at various breakpoints (word, after 2 letters, in numbers). Measure false-positive merges vs ground truth.
- Sample 500 real OCR outputs from last quarter, run auto-merge heuristics, then send 100 to labelers for manual review and compute agreement.

Implementation TODOs (mine / short-term):
- [ ] Add soft-hyphen stripper to pre-processing pipeline (low-risk).
- [ ] Implement alpha-alpha line-break merge with combined-length threshold = 4, run on staging.
- [ ] Create small keep-hyphen whitelist json (X-ray, T-shirt, state-of-the-art, well-being) and add to rule logic.
- [ ] Prototype column-aware check: use OCR block x-span metadata if available to avoid cross-column merges.
- [ ] Draft labeler examples and upload to labeling tool help text.
- [ ] Run small agreement study with Evelyn and Diego (assign sample set).

Open questions / notes to self:
- How often do we get multi-column layouts without block-level coordinates? If often, conservative rules only.
- Should we attempt language detection earlier to avoid merging in non-English docs? Yes, but budget the latency.
- For numeric merges, after joining digits we must run normalization back to human-readable format (re-insert commas for currency). Write test cases.

References / quick links:
- Slack thread: #labeling (Mar 5) - notes from Diego on weird invoice splits.
- GH PR: labeling-scripts/pull/78 has a preliminary merge script (needs tests).

Quick examples to paste into labeler help (copy-paste friendly):
- "trans-\nfer" -> "transfer" (auto-merge)
- "well-\nknown" -> "well-known" (keep hyphen)
- "1,234-\n567" -> "1234567" then normalize -> "1,234,567"
- "U-\nS" -> "US" (special-case acronyms)

If I don't return to this in 2 weeks, ping Evelyn in Slack and assign DATA-423.

-- Maya
